study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Meijer et al., Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Toward Understanding Autism Heterogeneity: Identifying Clinical Subgroups and Neuroanatomical Deviations

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The introduction and aims clearly state the objectives: combine clinical clustering with normative modeling to parse heterogeneity, test whether subgrouping increases neurobiological homogeneity, and evaluate classification performance. These directly satisfy the criteria of stating research questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "In the present study, we aimed to parse clinical and neuroanatomical heterogeneity in autism by combining clustering of clinical features with normative modeling..."; "we examined whether clinical subgrouping resulted in increased neurobiological homogeneity..."; "We further investigated whether the identified subgroups improved the accuracy of autism classification..."; "we aimed to investigate whether reduction in clinical heterogeneity would lead to a reduction in neurotomical heterogeneity..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: Using ABIDE I/II as the source, they cite the dataset and then detail exclusion criteria applied for the normative modeling analysis, including missing imaging, low image quality via Euler number threshold, corrupted preprocessing, missing FIQ, and site-size thresholds, and report the final NAI sample size used for modeling.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We combined the ABIDE repositories I... and II..."; "for the normative modeling analysis... (a) participants with lacking neuroimaging data... (b) low image quality as assessed by both visual inspection and the Euler number... we excluded individuals with values smaller than -300; (c) corrupted preprocessing... (d) participants missing FIQ information... and (e) sites with less than 10 individuals per diagnostic group... This resulted in a sample of 690 autistic and 744 NAI..."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The normative model includes age, site, FIQ, and Euler number as covariates, and intracranial volume for subcortical volume ROIs, addressing both demographic and multi-site effects by modeling site explicitly.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "We included age, site, FIQ, and quality measures (i.e., the Euler number) as covariates and additional intracranial volume for subcortical volumes."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The source of neuroimaging data for the reference cohort is explicitly ABIDE I and II, with citation and link to acquisition parameters on the ABIDE website.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We combined the ABIDE repositories I (Di Martino et al., 2014) and II (Di Martino et al., 2017)... Detailed information on imaging acquisition parameters can be found on the ABIDE website (https://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/abide/)."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data from existing datasets (ABIDE I/II) are used; per guidance, image acquisition protocol is not applicable and should be marked NA.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: They describe preprocessing with FreeSurfer v7.3.2, outline core pipeline steps, specify parcellation (Destrieux) and subcortical labeling workflow, and note more details in supplement. Quality control via Euler number is also described elsewhere.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "We processed the T1-weighted images... using the FreeSurfer software (Version 7.3.2)... intensity normalization, skull stripping... CT was extracted... using the Destrieux parcellation... To label subcortical tissue classes, we further applied the volume-based stream..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They use a hold-out validation scheme: train the normative model on 90% of NAI and test on the remaining 10% of NAI plus all autistic individuals, ensuring balanced distributions across partitions.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "The data set was split into a training set consisting of 90% of NAI and a test set consisting of all autistic individuals and the remaining 10% of NAI. We ensured that age, FIQ, and site were evenly distributed across the training and test sets."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No independent external healthy dataset beyond ABIDE I/II is reported for validating the normative model. The study combines ABIDE repositories and does not describe application to a separate external cohort.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: They specify the model type (warped likelihood Bayesian Linear Regression), key implementation details (per-ROI models, Z-score NPMs), and software/libraries with versions (PCNtoolkit v0.26, Python 3.9.16).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "Here, we performed normative modeling... using warped likelihood Bayesian Linear Regression (Fraza et al., 2021) model implemented in the PCNtoolkit (Version 0.26) in Python (Version 3.9.16)... A separate normative model was built for each of the 148 CT ROIs and 23 subcortical ROIs... Next, we computed normative probability maps (NPMs) consisting of subject-specific Z-scores..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model evaluation is stated, but quantitative performance metrics are deferred to supplemental materials (Figure S4) and not detailed in the main text available here.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "To evaluate model performance, we obtained state-of-the-art model evaluation parameters (see Figure S4 in the online supplemental materials)."
